sourceClaim: Retain foundational training while choosing complementary programs around time, recovery and purpose. The cited examples are not one universal schedule.
adaptation: For an explicitly selected core, reserve a fraction of actual opportunities equal to formal core program days divided by the opportunities available within the configured return window, capped at one. Use no faster than observed attendance, preserve partial-work priority and all existing gates. Bound ordinary consecutive core reservations to three while another block is ready. Protected-core plans respect the chosen total time budget without the legacy flexible extension.
limits: Formal program days do not prove movement-level feasibility when work is deferred or internal patterns rotate.
No generic biological minimum frequency, source-authored reservation ratio or universal kettlebell-first ladder is inferred.
Too many developing programs can still exceed capacity; this batch does not automatically remove saved programs or certify the rotation gate.
Forecast opportunity markers affect sequence only; they never count as earned actual work.
